items.response:
On it. I'll build a Khruangbin and A. R. Rahman instrumentals playlist for tomorrow (Tue 13 Jan), and swap spin for strength training at the Leslieville YMCA on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 6:15 am, with a note that you need to be home by 7:15 so Sam can leave for school. I'll leave a buffer for the walk or ride home so you actually make it back by 7:15.
Action: Build the playlist, find and delete the recurring spin events, create a recurring Tue/Thu 6:15 strength event at the Leslieville YMCA with a leave-by reminder, and flag anything on those mornings that clashes.

Here's a draft for the group chat:

"Hi neighbours! We're having a street yard sale on Sat Oct 4 from 9 to 1 (rain date Sun Oct 5). Set up your table on your own driveway, and please no early birds before 9, we mean it, lol. Come shop, sell, and say hi!"

Action: Wait for your edits, then you can paste it into the chat (I haven't sent anything). I'll also add the sale and the rain date to the calendar if you want.

Here's a tour checklist she can use for a 1-year-old: What are the infant/toddler staff-to-child ratio and group size, and is there low staff turnover? What does a typical day look like (naps, feeding, outdoor time), and how do they handle sleep and bottles or solids? What's the illness and sick-day policy, how do they communicate with parents day to day, and what are the fees, hours and start date? Also worth asking is whether they're licensed and when the last inspection was.
Action: Send her this as a short list you can forward to Marcus.

A cardboard fort is a great pick for a stormy day. Beyond the boxes you'll want packing or duct tape, a box cutter or scissors (adult-handled), markers or paint for decorating, and blankets or clips to make a roof. A flashlight or string lights for the inside, and some pillows, make it feel like a real hideout.
Action: Set a reminder tonight to bring the boxes up from the basement and check that you have tape, so you're not hunting for supplies tomorrow after school.

Done. Your call with your mother Anjali is blocked every Sunday at 9:00 am Toronto time (6:30 pm in Mumbai), recurring with no end date, and I'll treat that slot as busy so nothing gets booked over it. For Spanish, I'd suggest short sessions of 10 to 15 minutes between lessons with Carlos: first a quick review of what he covered, then a conversation where I play a role and gently correct you afterward. Tell me your goals and I'll shape it around that.
Action: Create the recurring Sunday 9:00 event with a protected status, then ask you when you're free for a first practice session.

I can't see live rink conditions from here, so I won't promise anything about Withrow Park rink on Saturday afternoon. I'll check the City of Toronto rink status and hours and the Saturday forecast, since mild temperatures can close an outdoor rink. That way you'll know before you plan skating after Leo's swim.
Action: Look up Withrow rink status and Saturday afternoon weather, and report back with a yes or a backup idea.

I don't have a confirmation for those in front of me, so I'd rather check than guess. I'll search your email and calendar for anything from the dentist about November appointments for you and Leo.
Action: Search Gmail and the calendar for dentist confirmations, then tell you the dates and times, or flag that none has come in and draft a note to the office.

Night, Riya, and congrats again on the launch.
Action: None tonight.

Glad that works. My pick for the mithai is Brijwasi Sweets: best freshness reviews (4.6 from 2,300 ratings), Rs 1,450 plus Rs 120 delivery, and same day if ordered before 14:00 IST. I'll need your mom's address to place it.
Action: Hold the order until you send the delivery address.

Got both. I'll remind you to send Tom your comments on the strategy memo before it's due Friday, and to pick up Leo's library books at the Pape branch on Saturday morning.
Action: Set a Friday morning reminder for the memo comments to Tom and a Saturday morning reminder for the Pape/Danforth library pickup.

RRSP: contributions are tax-deductible now and you pay tax when you withdraw, so it's best if you expect a lower tax rate in retirement than today. TFSA: you contribute after-tax money, and growth and withdrawals are tax-free, and you can take money out flexibly.
Action: None needed.

Saved under your health info, flagged as important:
- Penicillin allergy: hives
- Seasonal allergies in May: managed with Reactine
Action: Add these to your medical note and surface the penicillin allergy whenever a medication or appointment comes up.

I'd focus on speaking practice and reviewing whatever Carlos covered in your last lesson, plus a short vocabulary refresh, so the class feels like a warm-up and not a cold start. I don't have your class time or last lesson notes in front of me, so I'll check the calendar before blocking anything.
Action: Find the Spanish class on your calendar and last lesson's notes, then block 30 to 45 minutes of study time before it and send you a short focus list.

I'll look for one with no ads, no in-app purchases and no loot boxes. Two I'd check first are Lichess (free, no ads, no purchases) and ChessKid (built for kids, but the full lessons are behind a subscription), and I'd verify the current app store listings before you install anything.
Action: Check the current store listings and parental controls for both, then send you one recommendation.

25 minutes on the clock, happy gardening.
Action: Timer set for 25 minutes, starting now.

Told Hannah yes, we'll be there Sunday at 9 for pancakes. It's on the family calendar for Sun 8 Feb, 9:00, at Hannah's.
Action: Send the reply to Hannah and add the calendar event.

Scheduled the Slack message for #payouts-team for 9:00 tomorrow. For Priya, instead of 'follow your heart', some better questions: What would her day-to-day work look like in Toronto compared to now, and is it a step up, sideways or down? What would she be moving toward and what would she be leaving behind, including people, cost of living and housing? And can she say no, or reverse it, without a penalty, and is there a trial period or a deadline?
Action: Schedule the Slack post for 9:00 and turn the questions into a short message you can send Priya.

A useful way to frame it for Marcus: compare what the extra 10% pays against what the commute costs. Saving 35 minutes each way is about 70 minutes a day, which is roughly 5.8 hours a week if he works five days. He could ask himself what that time is worth to him, and also compare caseload, mentorship, growth and benefits, since a 10% pay gap can be small next to those.
Action: Draft a short message you can send Marcus with these points.

Ha, the classic office arctic blast. A cardigan or blanket at your desk is the cheap fix, and if it keeps happening I can ping facilities about the thermostat on your floor.
Action: None for now.

EFT (electronic funds transfer) is the general Canadian term for moving money electronically between bank accounts, for example direct deposit and pre-authorized debits, which clear through Payments Canada. ACH is the US network name (run by Nacha), and people in Canada often use it loosely to mean the same thing. So on that call they were probably talking about the same thing, but technically in Canada the correct term is EFT.
Action: None needed.

A HEPA air purifier with an activated-carbon filter is the thing I'd order for this, since the carbon handles cooking smells and the HEPA handles drywall dust. I'll find one in stock that can arrive before the week starts and send you the model, price and delivery date.
Action: Search for options with delivery before Monday and confirm the pick and total with you before I place the order.

I don't have last night's Raptors score and don't want to guess, so I'll look it up.
Action: Check the final score and send you a one-line result you can pass on to Sam.

Added: Toronto Waterfront Half Marathon, Oct 19, 2025, finish time 2:04:37, which works out to about 5:54 per km. I've tagged it for your December yearly recap.
Action: Log the race in your running stats and set a reminder in early December to start building the yearly recap.

Sent to Hannah. For NYE for five (Grace and Daniel arrive Wed 31 Dec around 15:00), I'd do a baked brie starter and a mushroom and spinach main, with nothing shellfish-based, and I'd double-check sauces for hidden shellfish, like oyster sauce. For Grace, a Pomegranate Rosemary Fizz: pomegranate juice, lime, rosemary syrup, topped with non-alcoholic sparkling wine in a flute so she toasts with everyone.
Action: Send the thank-you to Hannah, then write the full menu with a shopping list and prep schedule.

Reminder added. For the 1:1, you can't edit Tom's series since he owns it, but I can fix your copy so it shows Wednesdays at 11:30 starting in January 2026 and remove the Thursday occurrences from your calendar.
Action: Add the reminder, update your copy of the recurring 1:1 to Wednesdays 11:30, and check whether Tom's updated invite is already in your inbox.

For jammy yolks, lower cold eggs into already-boiling water and cook for about 6.5 to 7 minutes, then move them straight to an ice bath for a few minutes before peeling. For ramen eggs, a soy and mirin marinade for a few hours (or overnight) is what gives them their colour and flavour.
Action: Set a 7-minute timer when you're ready to start tomorrow.

On it. I'll search your email and notes for the Ottawa flights you looked at before deciding to drive, and open your podcast note so I can recommend shows based on what you like.
Action: Pull the flight options and put them in a short comparison for Sam, then send you a few podcast picks for the commute.

I can search your docs and the beta materials for links to the old pricing page and list every file where one turns up. I don't have the old pricing URL on hand, so I'll look for it in the docs, and if I can't find it I'll need it from you.
Action: Search Drive and the beta materials for the old link and send you the list of documents and where each link sits, without changing anything until you confirm the new URL.

Here's one for a 7-year-old: dogs are cousins of wolves, and wolves howl to talk to each other across long distances. The siren sounds like another dog howling, so Biscuit is howling back to say 'I'm here!' It doesn't hurt him; he's just joining the song.
Action: None.

You're welcome. Tom is still waiting on the link to the beta merchant numbers before his exec sync tomorrow morning.
Action: Set a reminder for after dinner to send Tom the link.

Jess should weigh a few things:
- Cash flow: will the rent cover the mortgage, fees, property tax and insurance, with room for vacancies?
- Taxes: rental income is taxable, and renting could affect the principal-residence exemption.
- Market view: selling locks in today's price, while holding is a bet on it rising.
- Effort and risk: being a landlord means tenants and repairs, plus transaction costs.
- Her plans: if she might move back, renting keeps the option open.
Action: None.

Yes, I'll take the data side. I'll pull the last 30 days of failed payouts grouped by receiving bank, with counts, failure rate per bank and the top failure reasons, so it's ready for Wednesday's roadmap prep. I'll confirm the definition of failed matches what the roadmap uses.
Action: Find the right report and start the pull, then send you the table and a short summary before Wednesday.

Enjoy dinner! The Kitsilano pool is open tomorrow from 7:00 to 20:45, with lanes closed until 9:00, so going after 9 works.
Action: None tonight.

Anytime. Enjoy the Biscuit snore-fest.
Action: None.

On it. I'll unsubscribe you from Old Navy, Wayfair, Uber Eats promos and Lululemon, and archive everything already in your inbox from them. The Dyson one you never signed up for I'd mark as spam instead of clicking its unsubscribe link, since that can confirm your address to a sender you don't know.
Action: Run the unsubscribes, archive the old mail, report Dyson as spam, and tell you if any sender needs a manual step.

A few that avoid hallmark territory:
- 'Thirty-one years of keeping this department running, and somehow making it look easy. We'll miss you.'
- 'Thank you for everything you taught the rest of us, on purpose and by example.'
- 'Thirty-one years at Riverdale and you leave it better than you found it. Enjoy every unscheduled day.'
Action: Send these to Sam and tweak whichever he likes.

Done: both items (Nate's backsplash decision and the February pizza lunch and Riverdale Farm trip form, all due Fri 30 Jan) are now on Thursday's to-do list. On the May trip, last year you noted an idea to take Sam's parents to the Canadian Tulip Festival in Ottawa in May 2026, with a plan to check the dates in April. Grace and Daniel are in Alta Vista, so you'd have a place to stay.
Action: Check the Tulip Festival dates against the May long weekend, and look for other kid-friendly events in Ottawa then. The Wen congratulations post is still unposted.

I'll rename the Scan_*.pdf files in Downloads using the date each was scanned, in a YYYY-MM-DD format, adding a number if two share a date. I'll use each file's own creation date and check it's reasonable before changing anything.
Action: List the files with their proposed new names, rename them, and keep a log so the change can be undone.

Regular mail from Toronto to Mumbai usually takes somewhere around one to three weeks, and it can run longer in busy periods, so I'd send it early. I don't want to quote a firm number without checking the current service standard.
Action: Check Canada Post's current estimate for letter mail to India and send you the date you should post the card by.

Told Hannah yes, Jun can come over Saturday from 1 to 4. For the rain, I'd plan three blocks: a Lego or building challenge with a timer, then a cushion-and-blanket fort or obstacle course, and finally a snack and a movie to end the afternoon, so you're not refereeing the whole time.
Action: Reply to Hannah, put Saturday 1:00 to 4:00 on the calendar, and write the activity plan into a short list for you.

Got it, I'll update Biscuit's contact to Dr. Kaur at Riverside Veterinary Clinic on Broadview Ave and mark Dr. Moreau as retired. My older note lists Riverside at a Queen St E address, so I'll confirm the clinic's location when I book.
Action: Update the vet contact, check next week's weekday openings after 5:30 pm for annual shots and the rabies booster, book the earliest, and add it to the calendar.

Here's a toast:

"Neha, you've always had great taste, and tonight it has outdone itself. To [partner]: you've chosen well, and you've been warned about the family. May your arguments always be about where to eat, never about whether to. To Neha and [partner]!"

Action: Fill in the partner's name once you send it, and tune the jokes to the family.

To triple the recipe, multiply every ingredient by 3, and the bake time per tray stays the same. I'm giving you metric measures and Celsius. I don't have the original amounts from 13 Dec, so I'll look for that chat; for Leo's tree nut allergy, keep any nuts out and check the chips' label.
Action: Find the 13 Dec conversation, and if it's not there, ask you for the bag's amounts and then send a tripled metric list.

I don't have this year's opening date for the Leslieville farmers market, so I won't guess. I'll check the market's website for the start date.
Action: Look up the opening date and hours, then add it to the calendar.

Here's what's left for Halloween night: Leo's costume (the cardboard box needs a finish), a treat bag, and a candy check. Leo is allergic to cashews and pistachios only, so sort through anything he collects before he eats it, and keep his EpiPen Jr in his backpack as usual. Also settle your route and timing, warm layers under the costume, and candy for handing out.
Action: Build a checklist with dates counting down to Halloween and set a reminder for the weekend to work on the costume.
